title: Progressive Revelation
definition: Progressive Revelation means God revealed His truth over time through Scripture, with earlier revelation preparing for the fuller revelation of Christ.
summary: Progressive Revelation means God revealed His truth over time through Scripture, with earlier revelation preparing for the fuller revelation of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus is the fulfillment and center of God’s unfolding revelation, bringing clarity to the promises, patterns, covenants, and hope of Scripture.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God did not reveal everything at once. Across history, He revealed His character, promises, law, covenants, warnings, and hope step by step. Each stage was true, but the fullness comes into clearer view as God’s plan unfolds.

Progressive revelation helps believers read the Bible as one unfolding story rather than disconnected pieces. The sacrifices, priesthood, kingdom promises, prophetic hopes, and wisdom of the Old Testament prepare the way for Christ and are fulfilled according to God’s purpose.

Jesus is not an afterthought added to Scripture. He is the One toward whom God’s revelation moves. In Him, God’s promises find their yes, and the Gospel becomes clear.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People can become confused when they read different parts of the Bible without understanding where they fit in God’s plan. Progressive revelation helps believers honor each passage while seeing the larger movement toward Christ.

This doctrine also protects against reading the Old Testament as if Jesus had not come or reading the New Testament as if God had changed His mind. God’s plan is unfolding, not divided against itself.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read Scripture patiently as one unfolding story of redemption. Ask how each passage fits in God’s plan, what it reveals at that point in history, and how it prepares for or flows from the finished work of Christ.
